title: Sports Dentistry Organizations Establish International Standards for Sports and Team Dentists
html:
By News Staff

November 16, 2026

Share

The Academy for Sports Dentistry (ASD) and the European Association for Sports Dentistry (EA4SD) have jointly released a consensus statement establishing standardized definitions of a Sports Dentist and a Team Dentist, along with minimum requirements for training, clinical competencies, and continuing education.

The statement is intended to provide guidance to physicians, athletic trainers, coaches, athletic organizations, school administrators, parents, and athletes when selecting dental professionals qualified to provide sports-related oral healthcare. It outlines competencies in the management of dental and orofacial trauma, return-to-play assessments, fabrication of protective mouthguards, recognition of concussion warning signs, compliance with anti-doping and medication regulations, and interdisciplinary coordination with sports medicine teams.

The consensus statement also defines the responsibilities of a Team Dentist as a Sports Dentist affiliated with an athletic team or facility. These responsibilities include conducting preseason and postseason dental examinations, maintaining 24-hour availability for dental and orofacial emergencies, providing on-site coverage during athletic competitions, and functioning within an established sports medicine team structure.

“The collaborative process is both stimulating and educational for all parties involved. Add to that the exceptional result, it is truly a WIN for all involved. This document will position Dentists to understand what is required to be a Sports/Team Dentist and serve as a guide for Sports Teams, our Medical Colleagues, Schools, Parents and Athletes themselves to better understand what the Dental profession can offer and along with guidance for selecting the most qualified practitioner to support the athlete(s)., said E. Jan Chithalen, ASD President.

“EA4SD underscores that a transatlantic alignment establishes a unified and universal framework for sports dentistry. Through this agreement, the definition of the sports and team dentist attains global scope, ensuring consistent standards of athlete care, sustainable integration into sports medicine, and solid development of this new science, across all continents," said Alessandro Nanussi, President of the European Association for Sports Dentistry.

The joint statement is intended to promote consistency in professional qualifications and clarify the role of dental practitioners in athlete health and safety across different levels of athletic participation.

The full consensus statement is available on the Academy for Sports Dentistry website.
